c1-gen-0036: Someone in the garden started asking questions. Let's read Genesis 3:1.
c1-gen-0037: After they ate, they tried to cover themselves. Let's read Genesis 3:7.
c1-gen-0038: The LORD God called to Adam in the garden. Let's hear what He asked, in Genesis 3:9.
c1-gen-0039: The woman took the fruit and ate it. Let's read what happened next in Genesis 3:6.
c1-gen-0040: Something changed the moment they ate. Let's read Genesis 3:7.
c1-gen-0041: They heard footsteps in the garden, and they ran to hide. Let's read Genesis 3:8.
c1-gen-0042: Adam's choice brought a hard word from God. Let's read Genesis 3:17.
c2-gen-0001: Cherubim and a flaming sword were placed at the east of the garden. Let's read why, in Genesis 3:22 and 24.
c1-gen-0043: God called Abram to leave home with a big promise. Let's read Genesis 12:2.
c1-gen-0044: Abram packed up and left Haran, just as God said. Let's read Genesis 12:4.
c1-gen-0045: God brought Abram outside and told him to look toward heaven and count. Let's read Genesis 15:5.
c1-gen-0046: Abram took God at His word. Let's read what the LORD did with that belief, in Genesis 15:6.
c1-gen-0047: God sent Abraham and Isaac on a hard journey. Let's read Genesis 22:2.
c1-gen-0048: The LORD promised Abram the land, and Abram responded. Let's read Genesis 12:7.
c1-gen-0049: Abraham was about to harm Isaac when a voice stopped him. Let's read Genesis 22:11 and 12.
c2-gen-0002: Abraham had told Isaac that God would provide. Let's see how that came true, in Genesis 22:8 and 13.
c1-gen-0050: Israel loved Joseph in a way the other sons could see. Let's read Genesis 37:3.
c1-gen-0051: Joseph told his brothers about a dream from the field. Let's read Genesis 37:7.
c1-gen-0052: Joseph's brothers pulled him out of the pit and made a deal. Let's read Genesis 37:28.
c1-gen-0053: Potiphar could tell the LORD was with Joseph. Let's read what job he gave him, in Genesis 39:3 and 4.
c1-gen-0054: Even in prison, the LORD stayed close to Joseph. Let's read Genesis 39:21.
c1-gen-0055: Joseph explained Pharaoh's dreams: seven good years, then a change. Let's read Genesis 41:29 and 30.
c1-gen-0056: Joseph could not keep his secret any longer. Let's read Genesis 45:1 and 2.
c2-gen-0003: Joseph looked back at all the hurt and saw God's hand in it. Let's read Genesis 45:7 and 50:20.
c1-mat-0027: Jesus was alone in the wilderness a long time before the tempter came. Let's read Matthew 4:1 and 2.
c1-mat-0028: The tempter tried to use hunger against Jesus. Let's read Matthew 4:3.
c1-mat-0029: The devil took Jesus to a very high mountain and made a show of things. Let's read Matthew 4:8 and 9.
c1-luk-0033: Jesus said people do not live by bread alone. Let's read Luke 4:4.
c1-luk-0034: The people in Nazareth grew angry and pushed Jesus out of town. Let's read Luke 4:28 through 30.
c1-jhn-0020: John saw Jesus walking by and spoke up. Let's read John 1:35 and 36.
c1-jhn-0021: Nathanael wondered how Jesus already knew him. Let's read John 1:48.
c2-luk-0001: Jesus read the scroll in His hometown synagogue, then sat down. Let's hear what He said next, in Luke 4:18, 20, and 21.
c1-exo-0010: Aaron stretched his hand over Egypt's waters, and the land was covered. Let's read Exodus 8:6.
c1-exo-0011: Each household had to choose a lamb, and God was particular about it. Let's read Exodus 12:5.
c1-exo-0012: Moses warned Pharaoh about the last plague and even named the hour. Let's read Exodus 11:4 and 5.
c1-exo-0013: The blood of the lamb had a special place to go. Let's read Exodus 12:7 and 22.
c1-exo-0014: God made a promise about what He would do when He saw the blood. Let's read Exodus 12:13.
c1-exo-0015: For a whole week, Israel's tables looked different. Let's read Exodus 12:15.
c1-exo-0016: Moses stretched his hand toward heaven, and thick darkness fell. Let's read Exodus 10:22 and 23.
c2-exo-0001: God protected His people while Egypt suffered. Let's read what He was showing, in Exodus 8:22, 8:23, and 11:7.
c1-jos-0001: God had a charge for Joshua before the big work began. Let's read Joshua 1:9.
c1-jos-0002: God told Joshua to keep something close, day and night. Let's read Joshua 1:8.
c1-jos-0003: Israel was about to cross the Jordan, and the priests had a job. Let's read Joshua 3:6.
c1-jos-0004: The priests' feet touched the edge of the river, and the water changed. Let's read Joshua 3:15 and 16.
c1-jos-0005: Seven priests marched in front as Israel circled Jericho. Let's read what they carried, in Joshua 6:4.
c1-jos-0006: For the first six days, the march around Jericho followed one pattern. Let's read Joshua 6:3 and 14.
c1-jos-0007: On the seventh day the people gave a great shout. Let's read what happened, in Joshua 6:20.
c2-jos-0001: God said He would begin to lift Joshua up in Israel's sight. Let's read why, in Joshua 1:5 and 3:7.
c1-jos-0008: The king of Jericho came looking, but the spies were already hidden. Let's read Joshua 2:6.
c1-jos-0009: The spies left Rahab with one clear instruction for her window. Let's read Joshua 2:18 and 21.
c1-jos-0010: Joshua had a special gift of land for Caleb. Let's read Joshua 14:13.
c1-jos-0011: Caleb remembered the other spies and how different his own heart was. Let's read Joshua 14:8.
c1-jos-0012: Rahab told the spies to hide in the mountain until the search party gave up. Let's read Joshua 2:16 and 22.
c1-jos-0013: After Israel settled in, the writer looks back at every promise God had made. Let's read Joshua 21:45.
c1-jos-0014: Joshua was old, and he gathered Israel's leaders for a careful word. Let's read Joshua 23:11.
c2-jos-0002: Rahab had heard what the LORD did for Israel, and it changed what she believed. Let's read Joshua 2:9 and 11.
c1-jdg-0001: The Angel of the LORD found Gideon at work with the wheat. Let's read Judges 6:11.
c1-jdg-0002: The Angel of the LORD greeted Gideon with a surprising title. Let's read Judges 6:12.
c1-jdg-0003: Gideon asked God for a sign and set something out overnight. Let's read Judges 6:37.
c1-jdg-0004: Early the next morning, Gideon checked his sign and squeezed. Let's read Judges 6:38.
c1-jdg-0005: The LORD told Gideon to send the fearful men home. Let's read how many stayed, in Judges 7:3.
c1-jdg-0006: At the water, the LORD sorted Gideon's men by how they drank. Let's read Judges 7:6.
c1-jdg-0007: Trumpets blasted, pitchers broke, and torches flared. Let's hear their cry in Judges 7:20.
c2-jdg-0001: The LORD said Gideon still had too many soldiers. Let's read why, in Judges 7:2.
c1-jdg-0008: Deborah was judging Israel in Jabin's days. Let's read what else the Bible calls her, in Judges 4:4.
c1-jdg-0009: When Israel came to Deborah for judgment, she had a regular place to sit. Let's read Judges 4:5.
c1-jdg-0010: Jabin made life hard for Israel for twenty years. Let's read about his chariots in Judges 4:3.
c1-jdg-0011: Barak would not go unless Deborah went too, and that changed the story. Let's read Judges 4:8 and 9.
c1-jdg-0012: Deborah and Barak finished their song with a prayer for those who love the LORD. Let's read Judges 5:31.
c1-jdg-0013: The LORD routed Sisera's army, and Sisera himself had to choose fast. Let's read Judges 4:15.
c1-jdg-0014: After the battle, Sisera ran to a tent he thought was safe. Let's read Judges 4:17.
c2-jdg-0002: Chapter 4 shows Sisera lining up his chariots. Chapter 5 sings about what swept them away. Let's read Judges 4:13 and 5:21.
c1-jdg-0015: The promised child's father lived in Zorah among the Danites. Let's read his name in Judges 13:2.
c1-jdg-0016: The Angel of the LORD gave one rule about the promised son's head. Let's read Judges 13:5.
c1-jdg-0017: The Angel of the LORD said this child would be set apart from the womb. Let's read what he would be called, in Judges 13:5.
c1-jdg-0018: Samson grew up under the LORD's blessing. Let's read what began to move upon him, in Judges 13:24 and 25.
c1-jdg-0019: The Philistine lords came to Delilah with silver and a request. Let's read Judges 16:5.
c1-jdg-0020: Samson sat in a Gaza prison, but something of his was growing again. Let's read Judges 16:22.
c1-jdg-0021: In the Philistine temple, Samson reached out and braced himself. Let's read Judges 16:29.
c2-jdg-0003: Samson woke up ready to shake himself free like before. Let's read what he did not know, in Judges 16:20.
c1-rut-0001: A family left Bethlehem and headed for Moab. Let's read why, in Ruth 1:1.
c1-rut-0002: Naomi told both young women to go home. Ruth held on, but the other one left. Let's read Ruth 1:14.
c1-rut-0003: Ruth promised that Naomi's people would be her people. Let's hear the rest in Ruth 1:16.
c1-rut-0004: Back in Bethlehem, Ruth asked Naomi for permission to go out to the field. Let's read Ruth 2:2.
c1-rut-0005: Ruth wondered why Boaz would be kind to a foreigner. Let's read what he had already heard, in Ruth 2:11.
c1-rut-0006: The closer relative gave up his right to redeem the land, and they sealed it the old way. Let's read Ruth 4:7 and 8.
c1-rut-0007: Boaz and Ruth had a baby boy, and the neighbor women named him. Let's read Ruth 4:13 and 17.
c2-rut-0001: That little boy grew up to be somebody's grandfather. Let's read Ruth 4:17.
c1-2sa-0001: David's reign as king had a starting age. Let's read 2 Samuel 5:4.
c1-2sa-0002: The elders of Israel came to anoint David king. Let's read where they met, in 2 Samuel 5:3.
c1-2sa-0003: The ark was coming up, and David gave the LORD everything he had. Let's read 2 Samuel 6:14.
c1-2sa-0004: David reigned over Judah first, then over the whole nation from a new city. Let's read 2 Samuel 5:5.
c1-2sa-0005: David lived in a cedar palace and felt the contrast. Let's read 2 Samuel 7:2.
c1-2sa-0006: Through Nathan, the LORD made a promise about David's throne. Let's read 2 Samuel 7:16.
c1-2sa-0007: David wanted to show kindness to anyone left of Saul's house. Let's read for whose sake, in 2 Samuel 9:1.
c2-2sa-0001: David wanted to build a dwelling for the LORD. The LORD had a different plan. Let's read 2 Samuel 7:5 and 11.
c1-2sa-0008: David's song of grief for Saul and Jonathan repeats one cry. Let's read 2 Samuel 1:19 and 27.
c1-2sa-0009: In that same lament, David spoke to Jonathan as a brother. Let's read 2 Samuel 1:26.
c1-2sa-0010: Absalom stood at the gate, shaking hands and kissing people who came for justice. Let's read 2 Samuel 15:6.
c1-2sa-0011: David left Jerusalem weeping, head covered and feet bare. Let's read which hill he climbed, in 2 Samuel 15:30.
c1-2sa-0012: News came from the battle, and the king went upstairs to weep. Let's hear what he cried, in 2 Samuel 18:33.
c1-2sa-0013: David sang after the LORD delivered him, and he started with a name for God. Let's read 2 Samuel 22:2.
c1-2sa-0014: In that same song, David said his God helped him leap. Let's read 2 Samuel 22:30.
c2-2sa-0002: Before the fight, David gave his captains an order about Absalom. That order explains a question he asked later. Let's read 2 Samuel 18:5 and 32.
c1-1ki-0001: God told Solomon to ask for whatever he wanted. Let's read what he chose, in 1 Kings 3:9.
c1-1ki-0002: Solomon built an inner room at the heart of the temple. Let's read what it was meant to hold, in 1 Kings 6:19.
c1-1ki-0003: The queen of Sheba traveled a long way after hearing about Solomon. Let's read 1 Kings 10:1.
c1-1ki-0004: God was pleased with Solomon's request and added gifts he never asked for. Let's read 1 Kings 3:13.
c1-1ki-0005: Two women stood before the king, both claiming the same baby. Let's hear the real mother in 1 Kings 3:26.
c1-1ki-0006: The temple stones were finished at the quarry, so the building site stayed unusual. Let's read 1 Kings 6:7.
c1-1ki-0007: Solomon kept building until every detail of the temple was finished. Let's read 1 Kings 6:38.
c2-1ki-0001: Solomon asked for help to judge the people. After the two mothers, all Israel saw something in him. Let's read 1 Kings 3:9 and 28.
c1-1ki-0008: Elijah walked in and spoke a hard word to King Ahab. Let's read 1 Kings 17:1.
c1-1ki-0009: Elijah hid by the Brook Cherith, and breakfast and supper still arrived. Let's read 1 Kings 17:6.
c1-1ki-0010: The widow of Zarephath baked a little cake for Elijah first. Let's read what did not run out, in 1 Kings 17:16.
c1-1ki-0011: Elijah carried the boy downstairs, alive again, into his mother's arms. Let's read 1 Kings 17:24.
c1-1ki-0012: On Mount Carmel, Elijah set a clear test between the LORD and Baal. Let's read 1 Kings 18:24.
c1-1ki-0013: Before Elijah prayed, he gave the people a surprising job with the offering. Let's read 1 Kings 18:33.
c1-1ki-0014: At Horeb, a wind came, then an earthquake, and still the LORD was not finished. Let's read 1 Kings 19:12.
c2-1ki-0002: Elijah prayed that the people would come to know the truth. After the LORD answered, they cried out. Let's read 1 Kings 18:37 and 39.
c1-mrk-0015: In Capernaum, Jesus commanded an unclean spirit, and the people were amazed. Let's read Mark 1:27.
c1-mrk-0016: Jesus took Simon's mother-in-law by the hand, and her fever left. Let's read what she did next, in Mark 1:31.
c1-mrk-0017: A man with leprosy knelt and trusted Jesus to make him clean. Let's read Mark 1:41.
c1-mrk-0018: Jesus freed the man who had lived among the tombs. Neighbors came and found him changed. Let's read Mark 5:15.
c1-mrk-0019: Jesus spoke to the Syro-Phoenician woman about bread and the little dogs. Let's hear her reply in Mark 7:28.
c1-mrk-0020: Jesus looked up, sighed, and spoke one word to a deaf man. Let's read what it means, in Mark 7:34.
c1-mrk-0021: At Bethsaida, Jesus touched a blind man's eyes and asked what he saw. Let's read Mark 8:24.
c2-mrk-0001: Jesus spoke peace to a woman who had been ill a long time. Then hard news came about a little girl. Let's read Mark 5:34 and 36.
c1-psa-0009: This psalm opens with a question the writer keeps bringing to God. Let's read Psalm 13:1.
c1-psa-0010: Psalm 27 starts by calling the LORD 'my salvation,' and then adds another name. Let's read Psalm 27:1.
c1-psa-0011: The writer pictures a thirsty animal longing for water, and says his soul is like that for God. Let's read Psalm 42:1.
c1-psa-0012: Psalm 27 ends with a charge, then says it again. Let's read Psalm 27:14.
c1-psa-0013: This verse tells us the LORD comes near to a certain kind of person. Let's read Psalm 34:18.
c1-psa-0014: The writer says God keeps track of his wanderings, and then he makes a request about his tears. Let's read Psalm 56:8.
c1-psa-0015: This verse says to trust God at all times, then finishes with a picture of who He is. Let's read Psalm 62:8.
c2-psa-0001: The same line comes back three times while the writer talks to his own downcast soul. Let's read Psalm 42:5, 42:11, and 43:5.
c1-pro-0009: This proverb sets hatred on one side and something stronger on the other. Let's read Proverbs 10:12.
c1-pro-0010: This proverb warns that too many words can lead to sin. Let's read what a wise person does, in Proverbs 10:19.
c1-pro-0011: This proverb says anxiety weighs a heart down, then names what lifts it. Let's read Proverbs 12:25.
c1-pro-0012: This proverb contrasts a talebearer with a faithful friend. Let's read Proverbs 11:13.
c1-pro-0013: This proverb says people fall where there is no counsel. Let's read Proverbs 11:14.
c1-pro-0014: Some words cut like a sword. This proverb shows what wise words do instead. Let's read Proverbs 12:18.
c1-pro-0015: The LORD hates lying, and this verse tells how He sees truthful people. Let's read Proverbs 12:22.
c2-pro-0001: Friends shape us, for better or worse. Let's read Proverbs 12:26 and 13:20.
c1-est-0001: The king sent for Queen Vashti to appear before his guests. Let's read how she answered, in Esther 1:12.
c1-est-0002: The king loved Esther more than all the other young women. Let's read Esther 2:17.
c1-est-0003: Esther walked into the court without being called, and the king saw her. Let's read Esther 5:2.
c1-est-0004: Everyone at the gate was told to honor Haman, but Mordecai would not. Let's read Esther 3:2 and 5.
c1-est-0005: Mordecai pressed Esther to speak up for her people. Let's read Esther 4:14.
c1-est-0006: Esther asked the Jews in Shushan to fast, then she faced the risk herself. Let's read Esther 4:16.
c1-est-0007: At the banquet, Esther told the king about Haman's plot. Let's read Esther 7:10.
c2-est-0001: Haman's decree brought mourning, but those days did not stay dark. Let's read Esther 4:3 and 9:22.
c1-mat-0030: Jesus said all authority had been given to Him, then He sent His followers out. Let's read Matthew 28:18 and 19.
c1-act-0025: An Ethiopian official was riding home, reading as the chariot rolled. Let's read Acts 8:28.
c1-act-0026: Philip and the Ethiopian were traveling together when the official pointed something out. Let's read Acts 8:36.
c1-act-0027: The Ethiopian stopped the chariot, and both men stepped out. Let's read Acts 8:38.
c1-act-0028: That very night, the jailer took care of Paul and Silas before his household was baptized. Let's read Acts 16:33.
c1-rom-0009: Paul says believers were buried with Christ through baptism, then raised to walk a certain way. Let's read Romans 6:4.
c1-gal-0001: Paul writes about everyone who has been baptized into Christ. Let's read Galatians 3:27.
c2-act-0002: After baptism, the Ethiopian went on his way. After baptism, the jailer brought Paul and Silas home. Let's read what both verses share, in Acts 8:39 and 16:34.
c1-1co-0001: Paul pictures the church as a body, and he imagines one part talking to another. Let's read 1 Corinthians 12:21.
c1-1co-0002: Believers have many different kinds of gifts. Paul says they still share something. Let's read 1 Corinthians 12:4.
c1-1co-0003: Paul tells them to desire the best gifts, then he points to something even better. Let's read 1 Corinthians 12:31.
c1-1co-0004: Paul says even the most impressive speech falls flat without love. Let's read 1 Corinthians 13:1.
c1-1co-0005: Prophecies, tongues, and knowledge will all pass away. Love is different. Let's read 1 Corinthians 13:8.
c1-1co-0006: Paul sums up the gospel: Christ died, He was buried, and then He rose. Let's read 1 Corinthians 15:3 and 4.
c1-1co-0007: Paul lists people who saw the risen Christ, and he starts with one name. Let's read 1 Corinthians 15:5.
c2-1co-0001: God put the body together so it would not split apart. Let's read 1 Corinthians 12:25 and 26.
c1-gal-0002: Paul says he has been crucified with Christ, and now Christ lives in him. Let's read Galatians 2:20.
c1-gal-0003: Paul lists the fruit the Spirit grows in a believer's life. Let's read Galatians 5:22.
c1-gal-0004: That same list continues into the next verse and ends with one last quality. Let's read Galatians 5:23.
c1-gal-0005: Paul says to walk in the Spirit, and then he names what you will not fulfill. Let's read Galatians 5:16.
c1-gal-0006: Paul tells believers to help carry each other's heavy loads. Let's read Galatians 6:2.
c1-gal-0007: Doing good can feel tiring, but Paul says not to lose heart. Let's read Galatians 6:9.
c1-gal-0008: Paul warns believers who bite and devour one another. Let's read Galatians 5:15.
c2-gal-0001: Believers are called to liberty, but not to use it selfishly. Let's read Galatians 5:13 and 14.
c1-rom-0010: Paul says believers have been justified by faith, and something follows from that. Let's read Romans 5:1.
c1-rom-0011: Because of God's mercies, Paul urges believers to present their bodies to God. Let's read Romans 12:1.
c1-rom-0012: Paul says not to let evil win. Let's read how he says to beat it, in Romans 12:21.
c1-rom-0013: Paul says not to copy this world. Let's read how he says to be changed, in Romans 12:2.
c1-rom-0014: Paul says believers can even glory in hard times, because those times produce something. Let's read Romans 5:3 and 4.
c1-rom-0015: Paul says to rejoice with people who are rejoicing. Let's read the other half in Romans 12:15.
c1-rom-0016: A body has many parts that do different jobs. Paul uses that picture for believers. Let's read Romans 12:4 and 5.
c2-rom-0001: That chain of growth ends with hope, and Paul explains why the hope holds. Let's read Romans 5:4 and 5.
c1-jas-0001: James tells believers how to think when all kinds of trials show up. Let's read James 1:2.
c1-jas-0002: James says there's a reason believers can face trials with the right attitude. Let's read James 1:3.
c1-jas-0003: James says anyone who needs wisdom should ask God, and ask in faith. Let's read James 1:5 and 6.
c1-jas-0004: James says hearing God's word is not enough by itself. Let's read James 1:22.
c1-jas-0005: James says to submit to God and resist the devil. Let's read what happens next, in James 4:7.
c1-jas-0006: James talks about faith that stands all by itself, with no works beside it. Let's read James 2:17.
c1-jas-0007: James pictures a large ship, and then he points to a tiny part that steers it. Let's read James 3:4 and 5.
c2-jas-0001: James points back to Abraham offering Isaac, then explains how faith and works fit together. Let's read James 2:21 and 22.
c1-jhn-0022: Jesus made a promise to anyone who comes to Him: they will never hunger. Let's read John 6:35.
c1-jhn-0023: Jesus said His followers would not walk in darkness. Let's read John 8:12.
c1-jhn-0024: Jesus compared Himself to someone who cares for sheep. Let's read John 10:11.
c1-jhn-0025: Jesus made a promise to everyone who believes in Him. Let's read John 11:25.
c1-jhn-0026: Jesus said no one comes to the Father except through Him. Let's read John 14:6.
c1-jhn-0027: Jesus said His Father is the vinedresser. Let's read what He called Himself, in John 15:1.
c1-jhn-0028: In that same sheep picture, Jesus said what He gives for them. Let's read John 10:11.
c2-jhn-0001: Jesus paired coming to Him with never hungering. Let's read what He paired with believing, in John 6:35.
